title: This pass's memory-hole classification produced the first non-none_of_these verdict in the practice's history: a compound-noun office title and an unlisted speech verb slipped past the ATTRIBUTION regex on a dropped press-feed sentence
statement: memoryhole/readings/2026-09-12.json (the newest reading; memoryhole/readings/2026-09-11.json does not exist, the disclosed permanent gap obs-2026-09-13-1.json already documented) carries 33 rule-layer abstentions across two institutions (bmg: 1, google-sustainability: 32) -- under the 40-per-night cap, so all 33 were classified tonight in memoryhole/verdicts/2026-09-12.json, this practice's second-ever verdicts file. The first, memoryhole/verdicts/2026-08-22.json, holds 4 verdicts; every one of those 4 -- the only verdicts that existed anywhere in the repository before tonight -- reads none_of_these. Tonight's 33 include 32 more none_of_these and one attribution_removed (before_sha256 2293ed19c74051149e9a82760db86aca02a9b4670fe30d73054dc007fcf68940, confidence medium): the first verdict of any kind other than none_of_these this practice has ever recorded. The passage behind that sha256 is a whole sentence present in the 2026-09-10 capture and absent from the 2026-09-12 one (a dropped RSS item, reflected in memoryhole/readings/2026-09-12.json's bmg entry as removed_tokens: 72, rewritten_pairs: 1). It reached classify_removal() in practice/src/practice/memoryhole/events.py (the keep_prose(diff.removed) branch, lines 195-207) rather than the aligned-pair branch, and classify_removal tests only two conditions on a fully-dropped sentence: salience.COMMIT and events.py's own ATTRIBUTION regex. Neither matched, which is why the deterministic layer abstained rather than emitting an attribution_removed event outright. The sentence names a federal ministry office holder by a German compound noun for that office and describes an interview they gave using a speech verb; ATTRIBUTION's word list requires \b-bounded matches on standalone tokens (minister, ministerin, sprecher, sprecherin, sagte, erklaerte, teilte mit, among others -- practice/src/practice/memoryhole/events.py, the ATTRIBUTION pattern), so a compound noun with the office-word in a non-initial, non-boundary position, and a speech verb outside that specific list, both fall through by construction -- not a bug in the regex's own logic, which the module's docstring already calls 'deliberately coarse' and tuned toward the safe direction under I8 (a false positive costs a passage its text; the risk the docstring names is over-redaction, not under-detection).
method: Read memoryhole/readings/2026-09-12.json in full, extracted all 33 abstentions (entries[].abstentions) and confirmed the total against foreknown-style figures (2 from institution bmg, 32 from google-sustainability). Located memoryhole/verdicts/2026-08-22.json as the only pre-existing verdicts file (ls memoryhole/verdicts/) and read every one of its 4 verdicts to confirm all read none_of_these -- the practice-wide baseline this pass's one exception is measured against. Classified all 33 abstentions per PROMPT.md's memoryhole-classify-routine-v1 instructions into memoryhole/verdicts/2026-09-12.json (cap 40, unclassified_at_cap 0). Read practice/src/practice/memoryhole/events.py in full (classify_pair, classify_removal, the ATTRIBUTION and COMMIT regexes, and classify()'s two branches) to trace exactly why a fully-dropped sentence with the salience signals named_entity+negation reached abstention rather than an event, and confirmed the specific compound-noun/word-boundary and verb-list reasons by testing the ATTRIBUTION pattern's \b-bounded alternatives against the sentence's own tokens. Read practice/src/practice/memoryhole/model.py's module docstring for the model layer's stated scope ('only abstentions reach this module... a verdict here is never merged into events') to confirm tonight's classification changes no committed reading, only annotates one. Ran python -m pytest practice/tests and python verify.py --repo-root . after writing the verdicts file; both green.
worth_watching_because: The observatory's own memory-hole rule layer is a fixed, disclosed word list by design, and this is the first committed instance of the exact failure shape that design accepts as a possibility: a genuine ascription to an office holder, in a sentence that was in fact dropped between two captures, missed by the ATTRIBUTION regex for structural reasons (a compound noun's internal word boundary, a verb outside the list) rather than by carelessness. It is one instance from one language's compounding rule interacting with one regex, in a module whose own docstring already names the direction it is tuned to fail safely in (over-redaction, not under-detection) -- not yet a pattern, since this is only the second night any memory-hole verdicts file has existed at all and the first had zero non-none_of_these verdicts to compare against. Whether German compound office-titles recur often enough in the watched institutions' feeds to be worth a dedicated rule-layer widening, versus staying a rare case the model layer's own discretion catches when it happens, is exactly the kind of question a single data point cannot answer.
left_alone: Not proposing a sensor: like obs-2026-09-12-1.json's constant 12-of-12 iso3 gap, there is exactly one instance and nothing yet to threshold a rule/model disagreement rate against -- a second independent instance of a compound-noun or unlisted-verb attribution slipping past the regex would be the point to consider one. Not editing practice/src/practice/memoryhole/events.py's ATTRIBUTION regex to add compound-word matching or the missing verb: unlike the memoryhole/run.py time-budget repair made on 2026-09-13's pass (which changed only scheduling and exception-handling logic around a fixed classification), widening the classifier itself changes what every future reading counts as an event versus an abstention, is exactly the kind of change events.py's own EVENTS_VERSION constant exists to version, and reaches further back than one night's abstention batch deserves to justify on its own -- left as an observation, not a repair. Not naming the office holder or the outlet's specific report content beyond what this file already states (I8): the verdict file itself carries only a sha256, a type, and a confidence, never the text or a name. Checked and left unchanged: sensor-resolution-reappearance-coverage.json (foreknown/registry.json's gdacs-tc-1001305 still OPEN, history unchanged since its last REVISED on 2026-09-03 -- no second closure); sensor-source-reconfirmation-blind-spot.json (gdacs-fl-1103815's datemodified in foreknown/snapshots/2026-09-13/gdacs.json still reads 2026-09-03T13:36:40, one more night confirming the freeze already tracked through 2026-09-12). registry-stall-check ran clean tonight (autonomy/log.jsonl, 2026-09-14T05:57:17, stale: []) -- memoryhole/run.py's 2026-09-13 time-budget repair is holding, with memoryhole/readings/2026-09-12.json itself the evidence (a real, on-schedule reading, not another skipped night).
